title: Best T-Shirt and Merch Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a T-shirt or merchandise designer: what the package should include, print files, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Merchandise design covers T-shirts, hoodies, mugs, stickers and more, for brands, events, creators and online shops. A design that looks good on screen must also print well on fabric or objects, in the method your printer uses. Orders go wrong when print specifications are ignored, rights are unclear, or the design copies someone else's work. This guide helps you order designs you can sell with confidence.

faq.q: Which file format does my printer need?
faq.a: Usually a high-resolution PNG with a transparent background or a vector file. Screen printing often needs a limited number of solid colors. Ask your printer or print-on-demand service for their requirements.

faq.q: How many colors can the design have?
faq.a: It depends on the print method. Screen printing charges per color; direct-to-garment and print-on-demand can handle full color. Tell the designer which method you will use.

faq.q: Can I sell products with the design?
faq.a: Only if you have the rights. Confirm in writing that the design is original and that you may use it commercially on products.

faq.q: Can the design include famous characters or logos?
faq.a: Not without permission. Using trademarks, characters or celebrity images on merchandise can lead to takedowns or legal claims.
